scenario_stem:
Briarfield Conserves Co is a private limited company in Country X making jams and chutneys at a factory opened 12 years ago. The business employs 85 production workers and produced 900,000 jars last year, with revenue of $2.7 million and profit of $270,000. Five years of rapid plant expansion has caused poor communication between the 3 shifts, and managers now report 140 jars rejected daily.

The board is choosing between two options. Option A is a horizontal integration: buying rival Hearthwick Conserves, producing 60,000 jars a month, for $1.8 million. Option B is organic growth: slowing expansion, adding 2 team supervisors and a written shift handover process, aiming to lift profit to $400,000 by 2029. Both plans target the same board deadline next autumn.

scenario_stem:

scenario_stem:
Redmoss Cider Co is a private limited company in Country X producing cider in an orchard region. The business buys 2,800 tonnes of apples a year from 24 growers at $900 per tonne, employs 70 staff and generated $3.6 million of revenue last year. After a poor harvest, apple prices jumped 25%, and 6 of its growers stopped supplying, forcing the mill to run at 70% of capacity.

The board is weighing backward vertical integration: buying 190 hectares of orchard for $3.8 million to secure its own apple supply. Alternatively, it could stay independent and sign 5-year supply contracts with 10 growers at fixed prices, keeping cash available for a planned production line upgrade next year. The harvest season begins in 5 months.

questions.model_answer: Productivity measures output per unit of input, such as output per worker or per hour, and rising productivity means the same resources produce more goods and services [2].

Problem 2: Idle capacity [k], because 6 of its 24 growers stopped supplying, forcing the mill to run at 70% of capacity with the same fixed costs spread over fewer tonnes [app].
